# CANDIDATE: VIX_FILTER_FAST_FALL

**Filed:** 2026-07-22  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Fast VIX declines often accompany false bullish breakouts that reverse quickly, causing losses on bearish setups. By filtering out entries when VIX falls rapidly, we can avoid entering bearish trades during short-lived bullish traps, preserving edge on genuine bearish days while reducing loser trades.

## Mechanism

At each potential entry bar, compute the 5-minute VIX change from the prior bar. If VIX falls by >= 0.5 points within the last 5 minutes, suppress the entry regardless of other signals. The filter applies only to bearish-side entries (PUTs) and is placed after the quality-escalation lock but before final entry decision, using the same bar timestamp as the trigger.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline.
2. **Sample bias:** No sample yet; proposed filter would be evaluated on full 16-month SPY 5m dataset (2025-01-02..2026-06-18) with look-ahead bias prevented by using only prior-bar VIX. Overfit risk exists if threshold is tuned to J anchor days; will use walk-forward OOS to mitigate.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward held-out window not yet performed).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (real OPRA fill simulation on top 3 J anchor days not yet performed).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: filter may suppress a genuine winner on a day with fast VIX fade but strong bearish follow-through (e.g., 5/04 if VIX drops intraday). Max drawdown scenario: filter fails to suppress losers during slow VIX grind, leaving edge unchanged. Blow-up scenario: none (filter only removes trades, never adds risk).
6. **Concentration:** Unknown until backtest; if top-5 days drive P&L, will disclose percentage.
